title: Central Long Island Native Communities
summary: A regional overview for Setauket/Setalcott, Secatogue, Nissequogue, Unkechaug, Yaphank, Wading River, and neighboring central Long Island communities.
content:
Central Long Island history is more than a line of separate town names. North Shore, South Shore, and inland communities were connected by rivers, ponds, footpaths, seasonal movement, kinship, labor, and diplomacy.

Setauket/Setalcott, Secatogue, Nissequogue, Unkechaug, and nearby communities appear in colonial records, place names, public gatherings, and present-day Native identity. Some records are deed-heavy, so they need broader context about continuity, land pressure, and changing colonial categories.

Public mapping in this region should stay broad for archaeological places, burial contexts, and private-property sites. Public schools, historic districts, public markers, reservations, and parks may be interpreted where sources and community sensitivity support it.
